subject: Hivemind dedicated sizing: SLA scaling exercise & safety matrix
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex@hivemind.ai>

Cc: ops@hivemind.ai

Subject: Dedicated sizing ask for upcoming commitment (MAU & peak profile attached)

Hi Sean / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo. Per our commitment discussion were trying to map the MAU / peak bursts into a Dedicated slab ask so procurement can sign. Attached is a CSV with hourly token volumes for our EU + US clusters and a separate sheet called "peak-scenarios" (we included BlackFriday-like / seasonal stress windows).

Target SLO: 95th latency <= 300ms for online chat (model: rw-4k-optimized-3B-quant). Typical prompt+response median tokens: 220 in, 180 out; tail sessions can hit 1500 tokens. Average active concurrent sessions today ~1,200.

Asks:
- Rough tokens/sec -> GPU mapping for the model (assume A100/80GB class).
- Headroom multiplier you'd recommend for a committed slab (we need a safety factor for bursts and model upgrades).
- Any ops constraints (warm KV cache needs, cold-start penalties) we should budget for.

Wed like a short spreadsheet/table and a 1-para recommendation we can include in our procurement packet.

Attaching: hivemind_mau_token_profile.csv (hourly)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if needed.

— Alex
Alex Park
Head of Platform, Hivemind.ai

Hi Alex —

Got the CSV, thanks. Quick read-through before we run numbers: a couple clarifying Qs that will materially change slab sizing so please confirm if you can:
1) Are the peak windows single-region or aggregated across EU+US? (we need per-region peak to size local slabs vs cross-region routing)
2) What concurrency distribution do you expect inside each peak hour? Is it short chat bursts (median 6s user think-time) or many long sessions holding KV cache alive?
3) Are you planning to enable streaming or return full responses at once? Streaming increases p95 tail for infra planning but reduces token-burst pressure across GPUs in some cases.

Ben / Irene — Ill ask you to do a first-pass tokens/sec -> GPU map. Ben, please assume A100-equivalent, RW-4k-3B quant, continuous batching optimizations and KV-cache enabled. Give a conservative per-GPU sustained tokens/sec and an estimated p95 per-request latency at target slab sizes. Include an explicit headroom multiplier for +50% peak bursts and a separate scenario for +150% BlackFriday.

Alex — once Ben drops numbers Ill produce a 1-page recommendation and a table you can slot into procurement.

Cheers,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

On Wed, Jul 28, 2027 at 11:12 AM Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Got the CSV, thanks. Quick read-through before we run numbers...

Alex / Sean — first-pass numbers below. Assumptions: model rw-4k-optimized-3B-quant on A100-equivalent with Redwood continuous batching and active KV cache. Sequence mix: 70% short (<=256 tokens total), 25% medium (256-800), 5% long (>800).

Conservative sustained throughput per GPU (tokens/sec): 1,300 tps
- Rationale: measured steady-state with batching and quantized kernels; short sequences are higher but long sequences reduce average due to KV lookups and memory bottlenecks.

Latency estimates (client-observed p95) at target slab allocations:
- Single GPU: p95 > 3s (not viable)
- 8 GPUs slab: p95 ~ 620ms (under heavy medium workloads)
- 16 GPUs slab: p95 ~ 310ms (close to SLO under expected concurrency)
- 24 GPUs slab: p95 ~ 220ms (comfortably within SLO with 25% headroom)

Mapping example (tokens/sec demand -> GPUs, before headroom):
- Demand 200k tps -> 154 GPUs (200,000 / 1,300 ≈ 154) -> use slabs of 16 => 10 slabs (160 GPUs)
- Demand 80k tps -> 62 GPUs -> 4 slabs (64 GPUs)

Recommended safety factors:
- Normal commit: 1.25x (25% cushion for daily burst variability and minor model changes)
- Aggressive retail/seasonal forecast (BlackFriday): 2.5x (to cover 90th-99th burst windows and warm-cache cold starts)

Operational notes:
- KV-cache warm-up: expect a 6-12 hour stabilization window after major traffic increases; plan for warm-up traffic or pre-warmed cache instances for cutover days.
- Cold-starts: scaled-down autoscale can present 5-10s cold latencies for first requests to a newly allocated slab; recommend reserved minimum of 2 GPUs per region for control-plane hooks to avoid total cold path.
- Quantization: 8-bit quantization is assumed. If you move to 4-bit aggressive quant, re-bench (throughput may improve 10-30% but variance increases).

Irene — I left the per-hour slab mapping to you with the CSV inputs; Ill sync if numbers vary.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <alex@hivemind.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

On Thu, Jul 29, 2027 at 9:07 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> first-pass numbers below...

Alex — I imported hivemind_mau_token_profile.csv and applied Bens conservative 1,300 tps per-GPU. Summary table (US region only, peak hour snapshot):

- Hour: 2027-11-26 18:00-19:00 (BlackFriday scenario)
  - tokens in hour: 9,720,000 -> tokens/sec avg 2,700
  - tokens/sec peak-window (5-min spike): 8,100
  - GPUs required (avg): 2,700 / 1,300 ≈ 2.08 -> round 3 GPUs (but rounding up to slab policy)
  - GPUs required (5-min spike): 8,100 / 1,300 ≈ 6.23 -> 8 GPUs recommended (one 8-GPU slab to cover spike)

- Typical daily peak (non-seasonal): tokens/sec peak-window: 3,600 -> GPUs ≈ 3 -> prefer 4 GPUs (slab-min)

Slab recommendation (per region):
- Base commit (monthly): 64 GPUs (4x16 slabs) — covers normal daily peaks with 25% cushion across hours when combined with autoscale burst.
- Seasonal buffer (Nov 20–Dec 5): allocate +32 GPUs (two additional 16-GPU slabs) to cover BlackFriday-like windows with 2.5x multiplier.

Notes:
- Because your peak spikes are short (5–15 minutes), maintain per-route burst routing so we don't overcommit across unrelated traffic.
- Recommend a canary period with 2 weeks of telemetry collection on the committed slabs to validate tail latency under real user mix.

I attached a small XLS with per-hour GPU counts aligned to your CSV (hivemind_proposed_slab_map_v1.xlsx). Please review and tell us if US/EU peaks must be mirrored or can be cross-region routed during off-hours.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround and the data. TL;DR recommendation you can paste into procurement: 

Recommended commitment (US region):
- Base reserved: 64 GPUs (4 x 16-GPU slabs) — supports expected daily peaks with a 25% safety cushion.
- Seasonal buffer: +32 GPUs (2 x 16-GPU slabs) for Nov 20–Dec 5 BlackFriday window; enable burst autoscale for additional short spikes.
- Canaries & ramp: reserve one 16-GPU slab for the first 2 weeks of production to validate p95 tail metrics.

Sizing rationale (single paragraph):
Using conservative per-GPU throughput of ~1,300 tokens/sec for rw-4k-optimized-3B-quant under Redwood continuous batching and KV-cache assumptions, the recommended base reserve maps to a steady-state capacity that meets the 95th latency SLO (<=300ms) in typical daily peaks. We add a 25% safety multiplier to account for short-term traffic variability, and a 2.5x seasonal multiplier to handle dense peak windows (5–15 minute spikes) where cache warm-up and burst concurrency drive transient token/sec demand.

Operational asks for procurement & ops:
- Contract clause for seasonal add-on slabs (short-term 30-day additions) to be pre-approved to reduce lead time.
- Monitoring: p95/request latency and per-slab token/sec telemetry with 15-min retention for the first 30 days.
- Pre-warm plan: schedule a 12-hour pre-warm before major promotions to populate KV caches.

Alex — if this is acceptable well produce a formal one-pager and include the attached spreadsheet for signature.

Best,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
